one_line: Nvidia faces leadership turmoil and export control scrutiny, Anthropic proceeds with its public offering, and major retailers take varying stances on AI shopping agents.

themes.title: Nvidia leadership and export control pressure
themes.text: Nvidia's board is reportedly preparing to oust CEO Jensen Huang following reports of extramarital affairs and links to an alleged Chinese spy. Meanwhile, new reports revealed that Chinese entities continued to access restricted chips through intermediaries, raising the likelihood of congressional export limits in the NDAA.

stories.headline: Nvidia stock drops as board reportedly prepares to oust CEO Jensen Huang
Nvidia board prepares to oust CEO Jensen Huang amid scandal
Nvidia spy scandal exposes Singapore chip networks evading US export controls
Jensen Huang affair raises chances of US chip export limits in NDAA
PLA-linked Chinese university obtained Nvidia H200 chips despite US blacklist

themes.title: Anthropic advances its public offering
themes.text: Anthropic opened its Australian retail initial public offering ahead of a Nasdaq listing, drawing multiple times the orders for its available shares. The company plans a livestreamed marketing event featuring CEO Dario Amodei and JPMorgan Chase CEO Jamie Dimon.

stories.headline: Anthropic opens Australian retail IPO ahead of Nasdaq listing
Anthropic IPO draws multiple times the orders for available shares

themes.title: Platforms restrict automated AI agents
themes.text: eBay joined Amazon in blocking unauthorized AI shopping agents from browsing and purchasing on its platforms, while United Airlines barred third-party AI travel booking agents due to data privacy and security risks.

stories.headline: eBay blocks AI shopping agents; Amazon, Target, Walmart take different stances
United Airlines bars unauthorized AI agents from booking travel
